why.text: Poor limestone, sand and gravel soils on Dordogne valley slopes, with a mild, damp Atlantic-influenced climate that ripens grapes well.

styles.text: Dry still reds and whites; rosés that are dry or off-dry.

climate.text: Attenuated oceanic climate, less rainy and a little colder than on the Atlantic coast. Summers are warmer and winters colder than at the coast. The funnel-shaped Dordogne valley carries Atlantic mildness and humidity nearly 100 km inland in spring and autumn. Wettest months are December, January and May.

soil.text: Poor soils: limestone rendzinas and brown calcareous soils, leached boulbène soils on sands, clays and molasse, and clay-gravel alluvial terraces. Limestone is marine Cretaceous upstream, lacustre on the left bank. They give good water regime.

tastes.text: Whites: floral and fruity with some acidity. Reds: fruity, sometimes richly tannic, a little austere when young. Rosés: often deeply coloured, dry or soft, always fresh.

styles.name: Clairet
styles.text: Deeply coloured rosé, mostly Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.

why.text: North-facing clay-limestone slopes above the Dordogne, where morning mist and sunny afternoons bring noble rot to Sémillon grapes.

styles.text: Still white wine with residual sugar, made from overripe grapes, with or without noble rot.

climate.text: Morning mist or fog followed by sunny afternoons favours noble rot (Botrytis cinerea) and concentrated grapes.

soil.text: Clay-limestone slopes facing north, on the left bank of the Dordogne.

tastes.text: Golden, darkening with age, elegant; aromas of honey, acacia and peach, with candied citrus and mirabelle plum. Sweetness is sometimes very high.

styles.name: Sélection de grains nobles
styles.text: Traditional mention that may complete the appellation, under the rules of the specification.

why.text: Limestone plateaus and Lot river terraces, with an oceanic climate warmed by Mediterranean summers and the dry Autan wind, suit Cot (Malbec).

climate.text: Oceanic with continental and Mediterranean influences; cold winters, sunny hot summers. Average rainfall is 700 mm a year, with a spring peak. The dry, warm Autan wind speeds ripening and dries the vines after storms.

soil.text: Jurassic and Cretaceous limestone plateaus, Oligocene and Miocene marl and limestone, and stepped alluvial terraces along the Lot. Soils give medium vigour; well-drained, easily warmed sites are favoured.

altitude.text: The limestone plateaus top out at about 300 m.

tastes.text: Deep colour when young; red and/or black fruit with spice; tannins can be very present. With age: dried fruit, truffle and a dense, rounded structure.

why.text: Well-oriented, free-draining hillsides of Pyrenean foothills with mild, humid, oceanic weather and warm dry autumns ripen late, tannic Tannat into dark, ageworthy reds.

styles.text: Dry still red wines only, blended mostly from Tannat.

climate.text: Mild, fairly humid oceanic climate: mild winters, cool wet springs. Slightly continental, with hot, often dry summers and autumns, and a warm dry foehn-type south wind about one day in three.

soil.text: Tertiary molasse (marls with some limestone) gives clay-limestone soils on steep west slopes. Acid, leached boulbène soils lie on gentle slopes and plateaus, where thick wind-blown silt covers the pebble layer.

altitude.text: Hillside vineyards on five parallel north-south ridges; altitude rises towards the south. No figures given.

tastes.text: Deep-coloured, tannic reds with good ageing potential. Red and black fruit, moving towards spice and candied fruit. Tannins soften with ageing into a balanced structure.

why.text: Foehn winds and steep slopes create sunny, dry, well-drained spots where thick-skinned local late grapes ripen fully, even raisin, despite a humid climate.

styles.text: Still white wines only, either dry or with residual sugar, including late-harvest wines.

climate.text: The foehn effect and strong slopes with cirques create favourable topoclimates: sun, warmth, low humidity and good drainage of rain. The wider climate is humid.

tastes.text: Dry: high acidity, lively, balanced by much richness, some age a few years. Sweet: fresh, not heavy; young fruity and floral, with age dried fruit and spice.

styles.name: Jurançon sec
styles.text: Dry white, at most 4 g/l fermentable sugar, label must say sec.

styles.name: Vendanges tardives
styles.text: Late harvest, no enrichment allowed, vintage must be stated on the label.

styles.name: Jurançon (sweet)
styles.text: Whites with more than 40 g/l fermentable sugar, picked by successive passes.
